chapter: The Famous Door, Billy May and the Palomar fire
title: Meeting Billy May at the New Penn Club
summary: Billy May arrived with an arrangement and the bored band sat up after eight bars.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: That's true. So consequently, any of these jobs you could get where you got radio time, like some of the biggest bands in the business took jobs in hotels and places, clubs that had radio time for unbelievably low money, because they would recoup it by going out on the road and then capitalizing on this exposure. So when we got to the New Penn, I had never heard of the New Penn, and as far as I'm concerned I hope I never hear of it again. It was outside on the -- it was like a roadhouse. And I think the Mafia owned it or something, because it was a rough place. But they had the wire. That was where I first met Billy May. We were having a rehearsal again, and here was this guy waiting there, and his shoes were cut out at the side to make it more comfortable, and he said, 'I've got an arrangement I'd like to have you try.' I told him the same thing, 'As soon as we finish what we're doing here I'll be happy to try it.' So we passed the arrangement out and the guys in the band, it was in the afternoon and they wanted to get out. They started groaning and I said, 'Well, let's try the arrangement.' We passed the arrangement out, and they were real drug and bored, and they leaned back and they got through about the first eight bars of the arrangement and they all came up in their seats and they were looking at the music, and Mr. Billy May was in.
